```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(data.table)
RES <- "results"; FIG <- "figures"
rd <- function(f) if (file.exists(file.path(RES, f))) fread(file.path(RES, f)) else NULL
img <- function(f) { p <- file.path(FIG, f); if (file.exists(p)) knitr::include_graphics(p) else invisible(NULL) }
kab <- function(d, ...) if (!is.null(d)) knitr::kable(d, ...) else cat("_(not available)_")
```

# Summary

This report documents a quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) model of covalent KRAS G12C
inhibition in previously treated KRAS G12C–mutant non–small-cell lung cancer. The model couples
oral pharmacokinetics, covalent engagement of a cycling (GDP/GTP) target, a lumped MAPK pathway
with adaptive ERK→upstream negative feedback, and a two-clone tumour (KRAS-dependent sensitive +
drug-tolerant resistant). It is calibrated to the published response and progression-free-survival
endpoints of sotorasib, adagrasib and docetaxel, then validated out-of-sample and used for in silico
trials and dose/schedule/combination exploration.

```{r headline, results='asis'}
hl <- file.path(RES, "headline.txt"); if (file.exists(hl)) cat("```\n", paste(readLines(hl), collapse = "\n"), "\n```\n")
```

# Target engagement, signalling and tumour dynamics

The irreversible inhibitor captures GDP-bound KRAS G12C; ERK suppression releases the upstream brake,
raising the activation input (adaptive reactivation). A typical sotorasib patient:

```{r}
img("fig05_target_engagement.png")
```

# Limitations

Effect-site is free plasma; the MAPK cascade is lumped to one ppERK output; resistance is two
compartments plus a pre-existing fraction, not an explicit mutational spectrum; calibration uses
summary-level published endpoints, not individual patient data. This is a research / educational
in silico model and is **not** a clinical decision tool.
